inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.question: Among interviews recording an approach by community or party representatives, how do the felt-threat and physical-threat reports distribute against interviews with no approach, and does the physical-threat report ever occur without a felt-threat report?
inquiries.alternatives: Approach present with threat reports at higher rate versus approach present with threat reports no different from no-approach, and the nested contrast of felt-only versus felt-plus-physical threat; either pattern would reframe threats as partially external-pressure rather than purely interviewer-experience events.
inquiries.ceiling: Restricted to interviewer-recorded Yes/No items in fieldwork; denominator is interviews where these items were asked and answered, not all contacted households; no claim about who approached, no causal effect of approach on threat, and no linkage to respondent answers.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Do respondents who grant the president latitude from laws and courts also accept military takeover when leaders abuse power, or does the rule-of-law position stand apart from the interventionist norm?
inquiries.alternatives: Concordant configuration (presidential latitude with takeover legitimacy) versus dissociated configuration (obedience to law among those accepting takeover, or latitude among those rejecting takeover); dissociation would show the two items tap separate normative commitments rather than one anti-constraint orientation.
inquiries.ceiling: Both are forced-choice self-reports with strength codes and neither/refused/don't-know states; not observations of presidential or military conduct; no country historical material accompanies the packet; eligible only where both items were asked.

inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.question: Within respondents, do the same actors get named for legislator accountability and presidential accountability, or does the president attract a different responsible actor than MPs?
inquiries.alternatives: Same-actor attribution versus office-contingent attribution where voters or party are named for MPs but Parliament or no-one for the president; office-contingent pairing would indicate distinct accountability models rather than a general civic-responsibility stance.
inquiries.ceiling: Nominal single-choice with shared actor list; denominator limited to settings where both items were asked; no inference about actual accountability practices, and refused/don't-know are not substantive actors.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Do respondents who expect community harassment of a woman candidate differ in effort demands on women's rights and in which issue they name as most important from those expecting little harassment?
inquiries.alternatives: Harassment-anticipating respondents concentrated on doing-more and a specific issue (e.g., gender-based violence) versus harassment-anticipating respondents showing no distinct effort or priority profile; either outcome separates anticipated social sanction from policy demand.
inquiries.ceiling: Cross-sectional associations only among asked-eligible respondents; no causal ordering between perceived sanction and issue priority; none-of-these and other codes retain their special meaning; no claim about actual harassment.

inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

inquiries.ceiling: Willingness denominator excludes the not-applicable neighbors without a mobile number; no claim about actual recontact, no verification of who really commissioned fieldwork, and other/don't-know sponsor codes retained separately.

inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.question: Is acceptance of police enforcement of health mandates distributed differently across interviewer-rated respondent honesty levels?
inquiries.alternatives: Mandate acceptance tracking honesty rating versus mandate acceptance flat across honesty ratings; a link would flag the emergency-powers measure as sensitive to interview rapport, a flat pattern would weaken that alternative reading.

claims.text: An ordinal binary record from the literal stem asking whether "you" were approached by community and/or political party representatives, where the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording; options are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only, with no detail on who approached or what was said.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: A binary record from the literal stem asking whether "you" felt threatened during the interview, where the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording; options are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: A binary record from the separately worded literal stem asking whether "you" were physically threatened during the interview, where the addressee is unresolved in the supplied item wording; options are 0 = No and 1 = Yes only, and no relation to the other threat item is asserted.

evidence.quote: Was he or she: honest, in between, or misleading?

claims.text: A three-point interviewer judgment of respondent honesty, running honest to in between to misleading, a perception of candor rather than an answer-accuracy test.

evidence.quote: should not be bound by laws or court decisions

claims.text: A forced-choice plus strength statement pair pitting presidential exemption from laws and court decisions against presidential obedience, recording a normative rule-of-law stance.

evidence.quote: should never intervene in the country's political process

claims.text: A forced-choice plus strength pair contrasting military non-intervention with legitimate takeover when elected leaders abuse power, a norm about the armed forces rather than an event report.

evidence.quote: [members of Parliament] do their jobs

claims.text: A single actor nomination from a fixed list assigning who should ensure elected MPs do their jobs, with options 0 = The President / Executive, 1 = The Parliament / local government council, 2 = Their Political Party, 3 = The Voters, 4 = No One, and special codes -1 = Missing, 8 = Refused, 9 = Don't know, 93 = Not asked in Burkina Faso after 4th of October, 94 = Not asked in country.

evidence.quote: the [president] does [his] job

claims.text: The president counterpart of the MP accountability item using the same actor list, so the two offices can be compared on one nominally shared scale.

evidence.quote: criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: A four-point likelihood that a woman candidate would face community criticism, name-calling, or harassment, an anticipated sanction rather than a recorded event.

evidence.quote: to advance the rights and equality of women

claims.text: A five-point effort judgment moving from much less to much more with about-right-amount in the middle, asking whether government action for women's rights is adequate rather than whether equality exists.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address?

claims.text: A single-choice selection of the most important women's-rights issue, with education, workplace, representation, property, violence, other, and an explicit none-of-these option.

evidence.quote: temporarily limit democracy or democratic freedoms

claims.text: A five-point agreement that police and security enforcement of public health mandates is a justified temporary limit on freedoms, conditioned on a public-health emergency and carrying a prior-COVID non-applicability code.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: A respondent attribution of the interview's sponsor across a fixed list spanning the survey organization, research and private companies, NGOs, schools, media, party, government, international bodies, God, other, and no one.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: A consent-style willingness for follow-up contact whose not-applicable code separates respondents lacking a mobile number from those who declined.
